benchmark.category: an Indian ride-hailing and vehicle-rental app (cab, bike, e-rickshaw, parcel courier, hourly rental)
benchmark.users: Indian customers booking rides/parcels/rentals, driver-partners who accept and complete trips, and a super admin who runs fares, drivers and bookings

requirements.statement: The app opens from a shared link in a browser: the root URL loads a working screen (landing when signed out) at 390px and desktop widths with no install and no login required
requirements.notes: The user answered the 'how do you want to open your app' question with 'Link'. The stated requirement is only that a link works; the landing-page contents are covered by derived requirements.

requirements.statement: GET / for an unauthenticated request returns the app shell with HTTP 200, and a deep link such as /book/cab or /admin/stats also returns the shell rather than a 404
requirements.notes: SPA history fallback; without it a shared link to a deep route breaks.

requirements.statement: A visitor signs up on /sign-up with an email and password and lands signed in; a second sign-up with the same email shows an error on screen and creates no second account
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of signup: the duplicate attempt must be refused visibly.

requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/signup stores the user with a hashed password and the role 'customer'; a second signup with the same email is refused and stores no second user
requirements.notes: Email+password sign-in is delivered through the auth provider in this build; the stored values and duplicate refusal are what Phase 4 checks.

requirements.statement: A registered user signs in on /sign-in with email and password and reaches the home screen for their role; a wrong password shows an error and leaves the user signed out
requirements.notes: Headless password sign-in may be blocked by bot protection; test sign-in through the provider's sign-in ticket for UI flows and against the session API for backend checks.

requirements.statement: Sign-in with the correct password returns a session token that authorises subsequent protected requests; a wrong password or an unknown email returns no token
Every account has exactly one role among customer, driver and super admin, and the server enforces each role's routes whatever the client sends
requirements.notes: Three-role model is the backbone of the access-control requirements.

requirements.statement: A demo super admin account exists in the seed data, signs in successfully and reaches /admin with the super admin role
requirements.notes: The user answered the super-admin email question with 'create demo' and named no address, so assert that a demo super admin exists and works rather than a specific email. Do not let another admin demote it away.

requirements.statement: Seeded super admin, approved driver and customer accounts each sign in and receive a working session whose role matches the seeded role, and the driver is seeded as approved with a vehicle type
requirements.notes: required_credentials names /app/memory/test_credentials.md and tests/seed_test_users.py admin|driver|customer. Every later phase seeds from these accounts. Return the driver to offline after tests.

requirements.statement: Every record the test suite creates carries the TEST_ prefix in its names and addresses so it is distinguishable from seeded and real data
requirements.notes: From the agent context note: 'Create any test data with TEST_ prefix in addresses/names'.

requirements.source_phrase: Car rides; Bike rides; E-rickshaw rides; Courier / parcel delivery; Hourly vehicle rental
requirements.statement: The signed-in customer's home screen shows exactly the five launch services — Car rides, Bike rides, E-rickshaw rides, Courier / parcel delivery, Hourly vehicle rental — and tapping each opens /book/:service for that service
requirements.notes: Tiles must render from the stored service catalogue, not a hardcoded list that drifts from what booking accepts.

requirements.source_phrase: Car rides; Bike rides; E-rickshaw rides; Courier / parcel delivery; Hourly vehicle rental
requirements.statement: GET /api/services returns the five launch services with their identifiers and pricing configuration, and POST /api/bookings with a service identifier outside that set is refused and stores nothing

On /book/cab the customer types a pickup and a drop, sees matching address suggestions, selects both, sees the two pins on a map and a fare estimate list, chooses an option, chooses cash and confirms; the app then opens /trip/:id showing the searching status
requirements.notes: Archetype of the ride-hailing product the user asked for ('like indian ubar'). The address/map/estimate/confirm chain is the primary flow of the whole app.

requirements.statement: GET /api/geo/search?q= returns a short list of matching place names with lat/lon resolved server-side through the OpenStreetMap/Nominatim lookup; a provider timeout returns a controlled error or empty list, never a 500 stack trace
requirements.notes: Third-party integration; Nominatim is rate limited (~1 req/s) so tests should use direct lat/lon in API calls rather than hammering search.

requirements.statement: Choosing a pickup and drop on /book/:service lists the fare estimate for each vehicle option of that service before booking, and each figure matches the value the server returns for that route and fare configuration
requirements.notes: Table stake of ride-hailing: the quote the customer sees is the price they pay.

requirements.statement: GET /api/fare-estimate computes the fare for the chosen service from the stored fare configuration (base fare, per-km, per-minute; hourly rate for rentals) and the route distance and duration, and rounds to the rupee as the configuration states
requirements.notes: Calculation inputs: distance km, duration minutes, fare config values; formula base + per_km*km + per_min*min (rental: hourly_rate*hours); rounding to the rupee assumed and recorded here as an assumption.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings validates pickup, drop, service and payment method, recomputes the fare server-side (a client-sent fare is ignored), stores the booking with status 'searching' and returns its id
requirements.notes: The server must be the source of the fare; a client-supplied amount overrides nothing.

requirements.statement: A customer with an active booking (searching, accepted, arrived or started) who creates another is refused with 409 and the existing booking is unchanged; after that booking completes or is cancelled a new booking succeeds
requirements.notes: Build states this rule and it is also an end-user expectation; tests must complete or cancel between bookings. The refusal must not create a half-written booking.

requirements.statement: On /book/parcel the customer must enter the receiver's name, phone and item description as well as pickup and drop; confirming with any of them empty shows a field-level message and creates no booking
requirements.notes: The parcel service is stated; the receiver/item field set is the shape of a courier flow and is stated as such here so Phase 4 can check it.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings for the parcel service refuses with 422 when receiver name, phone or item is missing, stores them when present, and returns them on the booking to the customer and to the assigned driver
On /book/rental the customer picks a pickup and a number of hours with no drop field, sees an hours-based estimate and confirms; the trip page shows the booked duration

POST /api/bookings for the rental service requires an integer hours value of at least 1, computes the fare as hourly rate × hours and stores the hours; hours of 0, a negative value or a non-integer is refused and stores nothing
requirements.notes: Boundary values 0, -1, 1.5, 1 (accepted) belong in the suite.

requirements.statement: A booking paid by cash is recorded with payment_method 'cash' and is marked payment_status 'paid' when the driver completes the trip, with the amount recorded equal to the booking's fare
requirements.notes: Cash must complete the whole flow with no Razorpay involvement.

requirements.statement: The driver's earning recorded for a completed trip equals the configured commission split applied to the fare (the build reports 80%), and the driver's earnings page total equals the sum of that driver's completed earnings only
requirements.notes: Build reports driver_earning = 80% of fare; the user set no split, so the split is recorded as the build's assumption while the sum-and-scope rule is asserted. A second driver's earnings must never appear in the total.

requirements.statement: An approved driver on /driver toggles online/offline and, while online, sees the list of searching requests for the driver's own vehicle type; opening one shows the customer's pickup, drop and fare
requirements.notes: The driver role is stated; its home screen is the archetype's supply side.

requirements.statement: GET /api/driver/requests returns only searching bookings whose service matches the driver's vehicle type while the driver is online, and an empty list when the driver is offline or unapproved
A car driver never receives a bike, e-rickshaw, parcel or rental request in /api/driver/requests, and a request for another vehicle type is refused (409/403) if accepted directly by id
requirements.notes: Paranoid inverse of the matching rule; over-broad matching would hand a parcel to a cab driver.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings/{id}/accept assigns the booking to exactly one driver; a concurrent or later accept by another driver is refused and does not change the assigned driver
requirements.notes: Build claims an atomic accept; test a race with two drivers on one request.

requirements.statement: A driver already on an active trip is not offered new requests and is refused when accepting one directly, leaving the existing trip unchanged
POST /api/bookings/{id}/start requires the customer's trip OTP; a wrong OTP returns 400 and leaves the booking in 'arrived', and the correct OTP moves it to 'started'
requirements.notes: Starting without the OTP, with an empty OTP, or with another booking's OTP must all be refused.

requirements.statement: No driver-facing response (requests list, accept, arrived, start, complete) includes the trip OTP, and no response for a booking the caller does not own returns it; the OTP is readable only by that booking's customer once a driver has accepted
requirements.notes: Privacy boundary of the product; asserted from the user's demand for a professional, real-world app. A guessed booking id and a direct link must also be refused for non-owners.

requirements.statement: The customer's /trip/:id page shows the trip OTP once a driver has accepted the booking and does not show it before acceptance

The customer's /trip/:id page shows the booking's status at each step (searching, accepted, arrived, started, completed) together with the driver's name and vehicle after acceptance, updating without a manual reload
GET /api/bookings/{id} returns the booking's current status, driver and payment fields to its owner, and each status transition is persisted so a request in a fresh session returns the latest state
After a trip completes the customer rates it 1–5 on the trip page and sees the rating recorded, and the driver's displayed average rating changes accordingly

POST /api/bookings/{id}/rating stores one integer 1–5 per completed booking, refuses a rating on a non-completed or another user's booking, and recomputes the driver's average from all that driver's ratings
A signed-in customer applies to become a driver at /driver/apply with vehicle details, sees a pending state, and cannot take rides until approved

POST /api/driver/apply stores the application as pending and leaves the user's role as customer; the role becomes driver only when a super admin approves, and driver endpoints return 403 for a pending applicant
The super admin's /admin/stats screen shows counts of users by role, bookings by status and completed revenue that match the stored data
GET /api/admin/stats returns counts and totals computed from the database (users by role, bookings by status, sum of completed fares) and returns 403 for a non-admin
The super admin's /admin/bookings lists all customers' bookings and filters by status and by service, and the filtered list matches exactly the stored bookings
GET /api/admin/bookings with a status or service filter returns exactly the matching bookings across all customers and is paginated; an unknown filter value returns an empty list, not an error
requirements.notes: Filter must offer every value the stored data holds, whatever the screen lists today.

requirements.statement: The super admin edits a service's pricing on /admin/fares, saves, and the new values are shown again after a reload and used by the next fare estimate

PUT /api/admin/fares persists validated non-negative numeric fare values; a negative or non-numeric value is refused with nothing written, subsequent estimates use the stored values, and existing bookings keep their original fare
requirements.notes: Editing fares must move future quotes and never retro-price a booking already made.

requirements.statement: The super admin changes a user's role on /admin/users and the change is reflected after reload; an action that would remove the last super admin is refused with an explanation on screen
PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role validates the role value, persists it, and refuses with 409 a change that would leave zero super admins

A valid customer token gets 403 on GET /api/admin/stats and on every /api/admin route, no token gets 401 on any protected endpoint, a customer requesting another customer's booking id gets 404 with no field of that booking, and driver endpoints return 403 for a customer
requirements.notes: The user's 'make it compatible with real world and a professional app' lands here as the access-control boundary; test both the refusal and the legitimate owner's succeeding 200.

requirements.statement: At checkout the customer sees cash and online (Razorpay) payment options; cash always works, and while no Razorpay keys are configured the online option is shown disabled with the reason and cannot be selected
requirements.notes: The user selected Razorpay and cash; the key question was skipped, so a disabled-but-explained online option is the expected state, not a bug.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings with payment_method 'online' returns 422 while Razorpay keys are unset, and when keys are set creates a Razorpay order whose amount equals the booking fare to the rupee and stores the order id
requirements.notes: With no keys the refusal must come from the server, not only from a disabled button.

requirements.statement: A booking is marked online-paid only after the server verifies the Razorpay signature against its own secret and records the payment once; a failed or unverified payment leaves the booking unpaid and returns an error the screen shows
requirements.notes: Payments class: server-computed amount, confirmation before access, exactly once. Without test keys this is checked by code path and by the 422 refusal.

requirements.statement: Signing out returns the user to the signed-out landing screen, and the app then makes no further signed-in requests
requirements.notes: Session class; watch network calls after sign-out.

requirements.statement: After sign-out the previous session token is rejected with 401 by protected endpoints and no cached signed-in data is served to that token
Reloading /trip/:id, or opening it again in a new session, shows the same booking with the same status, fare and driver
requirements.notes: Persistence across reload and new session.

requirements.statement: GET /api/bookings/{id} from a freshly issued session of the booking's customer returns identical fare, status and pickup/drop to what was written at creation
A customer with no active booking sees an explicit empty state rather than a blank panel or endless spinner, and an admin with no matching bookings sees an empty-list message
GET /api/bookings for a customer with no bookings returns an empty array with 200, and GET /api/admin/bookings on an empty database returns an empty page with total 0
The customer cancels from /trip/:id while the booking is searching, accepted or arrived, and the page then shows the cancelled status

POST /api/bookings/{id}/cancel succeeds for searching, accepted and arrived bookings and persists status 'cancelled'; cancelling a started or completed booking is refused with the status unchanged, and a cancelled booking no longer blocks a new booking
requirements.notes: Refusal after the trip starts is the paranoid half; over-refusal of early cancel would strand the customer.

requirements.statement: POST rating with 0, 6, a non-integer or a missing value is refused with 422 and stores no rating, and the same customer rating the same booking twice does not create two ratings

Every screen renders readable, unclipped content at 390px width with the bottom tab bar and at desktop width with the header nav, and each screen's primary action is reachable without horizontal scrolling
requirements.notes: The user asked for a mobile app delivered as a link; the build serves both widths. Check landing, booking, trip, driver and admin screens at both.

requirements.statement: GET /api/me returns the signed-in user's id, name and role, and the client renders its navigation from it; an unauthenticated request returns 401 and the client shows the signed-out shell
requirements.notes: The shell shows different tabs for customer, driver and admin; that decision must come from the server session.

requirements.statement: Every failed action (booking, cancel, accept, start with a wrong OTP, fare save, role change) shows the server's error message on screen and leaves the visible state unchanged
A refused write (409, 422 or 403) leaves no partial record — a refused booking creates no booking, a refused fare save changes no fare, a refused role change alters no role
An expired, malformed or invalid token returns 401 rather than 500 on every protected endpoint, and a role change made by an admin takes effect on that user's next request
The fare, status, payment method and payment status shown on /trip/:id and in /admin/bookings equal the values stored on the booking document at that moment
requirements.notes: Data class: what a screen shows must equal what is stored, checked by reading the record directly.

requirements.statement: When the address search provider is slow or errors, /book/:service shows a message and the customer can still set pickup and drop (map point or coordinates); the screen never hangs on a spinner
GET /api/geo/search returns a controlled empty result or a handled error on Nominatim failure or timeout, keeps its call rate at about one request per second, and never exposes a stack trace
requirements.notes: Third-party integration: the provider is public and rate limited, which is why tests use direct lat/lon.

requirements.statement: While online, a newly created matching request appears in the driver's request list within a few seconds without a manual refresh, and a request the driver cannot serve never appears
requirements.notes: benchmark: ride-hailing driver apps push a new request to nearby online drivers within seconds; the build implements it by polling.

requirements.statement: A customer sees a list of their past bookings with date, service, fare and status, and another customer's bookings never appear in it
requirements.notes: benchmark: ride-hailing apps give every rider a ride history; the app's /trips surface carries it.

requirements.statement: GET /api/bookings for a signed-in customer returns only that customer's bookings ordered newest first, paginated, with no other customer's ids present
requirements.notes: benchmark: ride-hailing ride history is scoped to the rider.

requirements.statement: Reopening /admin/bookings or /trips does not leak timers or connections (no runaway repeated polling), and a dataset of a thousand bookings still loads one page at a time with a working next-page control
requirements.notes: Performance and resource leaks class.

requirements.statement: GET /api/admin/bookings and GET /api/bookings return a bounded page with a total count instead of the whole collection, and a page over a thousand stored bookings returns within normal latency

The backend reads its Mongo URI, auth-provider secret and Razorpay keys from environment variables, starts and serves every screen with the Razorpay keys absent (online payments disabled, cash working), and ships no secret in the client bundle
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class; the Razorpay keys were skipped, so boot without them is the required behaviour.

requirements.statement: The deployed link loads every route (landing, /sign-up, /sign-in, /book/:service, /trip/:id, /driver, /driver/apply, /admin/stats, /admin/bookings, /admin/fares, /admin/users) for the right role with no build error, blank screen or console exception
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class: the deployed app must behave like the preview.

unmapped_phrases.reason: no objective specification on its own; its testable content is carried by the access-control, privacy and responsive requirements

unmapped_phrases.phrase: make it compatible with real world and a professional app
unmapped_phrases.reason: no objective specification; the real-world behaviours it implies are written as the OTP privacy, authorization, duplicate-refusal and persistence requirements
technology choice, not user-observable behaviour; the observable part is covered by the persistence and API requirements
the user skipped the Razorpay key question, so no keys exist; the resulting disabled online payment is covered by payment-methods-fe and payment-online-be and is not a defect
